1995.simple: A big network’s router: a tall cupboard full of cards, each joined to a long line. It reads the address on every parcel and picks the line that brings it closer.
1995.technical: A 1990s backbone router: a chassis of line cards (T1/E1, T3, ATM OC-3) with a route processor running BGP. It looks up every packet’s destination in its table, with no MPLS labels yet (they came around 2001).
